symptom: In a workflow, `call microflow M.ACT_Bind(Workflow = $Workflow, Item = $WorkflowContext);` passed `check --references` and `exec`, then mx check failed CE0117 "Error(s) in expression." (mendixlabs/mxcli#1529). The unmapped-parameter error for a System.Workflow parameter suggested the deprecated `with (Workflow = ...)` and never said what to pass, so authors guessed $Workflow; with no argument list, auto-bind mapped EVERY parameter to $WorkflowContext, so a System.Workflow parameter got the context object (mendixlabs/mxcli#1523).
cause: No workflow rule looked at the variables an expression names: MDL-WF01..17 check structure, and the writer only rewrote the context's spelling. Code comments asserted 'the only in-scope variable is the context' — wrong: $WorkflowInstance (System.Workflow) is in scope too, and appeared nowhere in Go code or skills. The writer also skipped boundary timers, event sub-process timer starts, call-workflow arguments and the header due date when rewriting the declared context name, so `$Ctx` there reached Mendix verbatim.
fix: MDL-WF19 (validate_workflow_scope.go): scan $names outside string literals in every workflow expression (call microflow/workflow arguments, decision, wait for timer, user task due date, boundary timers, ESP timer start, header due date; ALTER's inserts, boundary delay and set due_date) — allowed: any case of WorkflowContext, the declared header name, and WorkflowInstance except in the header due date; refused at check and at exec. Auto-bind maps a System.Workflow parameter to $WorkflowInstance; the unmapped message names the current `call microflow M(P = value)` form with a type-aware value. The writer normalizes the context alias/casing and $WorkflowInstance casing at every expression site.
insight: The scope table was settled by one mx check run per expression kind on 11.6.6 and 11.15.0 (identical): $WorkflowInstance builds everywhere EXCEPT the workflow's own due date (evaluated before the instance exists); $Workflow, $currentUser, $currentSession and $WorkflowUserTask are CE0117 everywhere; lower-case $workflowInstance is CE0117 as stored. mx check reports CE0117 'at Decision ''Decision''' / 'at User task ''U''', not per document, so give every probe activity a distinct caption or the verdicts cannot be attributed. A 'which variables are in scope' rule is only false-positive-safe when the writer's rewrites and the rule's allow-list are the same set — they had drifted (alias rewritten in a decision, written verbatim in a boundary timer), so the fix had to close the writer gap before the allow-list was honest.
